conventions.convention: The prior is a Borel probability on a separable real Banach space, the forward domain D is Borel with prior mass one, and restriction to D uses its trace Borel sigma-algebra.
Potentials take values in (−∞,+∞], exclude −∞, and use exp(−∞)=0. A normalized fiberwise update is defined only when evidence is strictly positive and finite.

Fixed-data normalization alone asserts no conditional-law interpretation. The dominated-model branch requires a proper sampling kernel, a sigma-finite dominating data measure and a specified jointly measurable density; it fills zero and infinite evidence fibers with the prior.

The separate posterior-kernel existence branch assumes AC and standard-Borel parameter and data spaces. Kernel uniqueness is outside one data-marginal-null set; null-fiber values remain version choices.

On the asserted data set, every potential section is finite and continuous in the relative topology. One nonnegative Borel radial lower envelope, independent of the datum, has integrable exponential. The conclusion is pointwise for every datum in that set, without requiring that set to be measurable.
The improper-prior example uses N={0,1,2,…}, counting measure of infinite total mass, and datum y=0. Its normalized probability is a fixed-data update, without a prior-predictive probability.

load_bearing.statement: For a jointly measurable potential Φ:D×Y→(−∞,+∞], define LΦ(u;y)=exp(−Φ(u;y)) and ZΦ(y)=∫D LΦ(u;y) μ0,D(du). For each fixed y with 0<ZΦ(y)<∞, define Πy(A)=∫A LΦ(u;y) μ0,D(du)/ZΦ(y). No normalized fiberwise update is defined by this formula at zero or infinite evidence. Its conditional-law interpretation requires the separately specified observation model and version convention.

Let X be a separable real Banach space, D⊆X Borel, μ0 a Borel probability with μ0(D)=1, and Φ:D×Y→(−∞,+∞] jointly measurable. For every y∈Y0 suppose Φ(·;y) is finite and continuous on D. Suppose one Borel M1:[0,∞)→[0,∞), independent of y∈Y0, satisfies Φ(u;y)≥−M1(‖u‖X) and ∫D exp(M1(‖u‖X)) μ0,D(du)<∞. Then for every y∈Y0 the evidence is finite and strictly positive, and the normalized fiberwise update is a probability measure on D.

seams_checked.note: The actual supplier is def-ip-prior-on-a-forward-domain. The consumer preserves the Borel full-mass domain and probability restriction; no stronger regularity or Gaussian-support conclusion is imported.

Both stability theorems supply finite continuous potentials and integrable common lower envelopes. They correctly conclude pointwise positive finite evidence and distinguish fixed-data updates from conditional-law versions.

The finite Gaussian posterior theorem uses a continuous nonnegative potential, the zero lower envelope and a proper finite-dimensional prior. It separately identifies the conditional version and allows singular prior covariance.
The MAP theorem constructs M1(t)=max(0,εt²−Mε), verifies its exponential integrability using the stated Gaussian moment supplier, and applies propriety with one datum and the whole Banach domain.

The page prerequisite is contextual rather than a direct citation of the two assigned suppliers. The contraction definition supplies a proper prior and posterior-kernel identities, and explicitly fixes the version used under the truth-specific data law.
The credible-set definition takes a proper prior and a supplied posterior probability kernel. It does not infer frequentist coverage or pointwise kernel uniqueness from posterior propriety.

The algorithm explicitly assumes positive finite evidence and handles infinite potentials by extension. The small-step theorem supplies a finite continuous nonnegative potential and hence an integrable zero envelope; invariance asserts no mixing or convergence guarantee.

The finite-dimensional conditional-kernel uses retain AC, standard-Borel spaces and almost-everywhere version qualifications. Exact posterior transport requires the separately assumed exact joint pushforward identity.
The learned-estimator definition distinguishes point maps, learned priors and sampling kernels. Exactness is relative to a supplied posterior target kernel on a declared data domain.

The design experiment supplies a proper prior, sigma-finite domination and jointly measurable sampling densities. Posterior ratios are restricted to positive finite evidence fibers, with exceptional fibers excluded from the EIG integral.
